mechanism_narrative: The observed sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the last four weeks indicates a continued recovery in consumer activity, driving further increases in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days in more than 50% of instances where RETAIL_REC showed a sustained upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: As residential mobility continues its recent decline, it signifies a shift in daily routines where more individuals are spending time outside their homes, directly translating to increased engagement with retail and recreation venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.5% in the current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a strong return to office-based work and associated commuting, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation activity during lunch breaks and after-work hours, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based increase across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) suggests an underlying policy-driven easing of restrictions or a strong public sentiment towards reopening, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, indicating a reversal of the reopening trend, despite other proxies remaining positive.

mechanism_narrative: The significant and sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates a growing public comfort with out-of-home activities, which will naturally extend to more discretionary retail and recreation spending over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next 7 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated or increasing.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS mobility from its dip suggests improved weather or increased leisure activity, which often precedes or coincides with increased foot traffic in other outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation areas, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 14 days, despite PARKS showing a week-on-week increase greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: If the rate of increase in WORKPLACES mobility significantly slows while RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its decline, it suggests a shift where fewer people are commuting to work but are also not staying home, potentially indicating out-migration or engagement in activities not captured by RETAIL_REC, leading to a slight decrease in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change < 1.0 AND RESIDENTIAL week-on-week change < -0.5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite WORKPLACES growth slowing to less than 1.0 point week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL continuing to fall by more than 0.5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and simultaneous recovery observed across all 'out-of-home' mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) indicates a robust and widespread return to pre-pandemic activity levels, which will continue to propel RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean of the last 28 days, despite all listed proxies showing continued recovery.
